analysis.investment_thesis: Cyient is a capable engineering services business serving aerospace, defense, and utilities clients, but services businesses without proprietary IP rarely sustain pricing power — the 9% operating margin and 12.8% ROE confirm this reality. With earnings declining in FY25 (net profit INR 703 Cr → 648 Cr) and promoter holding at a low 23.28%, I see no durable competitive advantage worth paying for.
key_strengths: Near debt-free balance sheet (D/E 0.07) with FCF positive every year, including INR 688 Cr in FY25
Exposure to long-cycle aerospace, defense, and rail programs creates multi-year contract visibility and some switching costs
Forward P/E of 14.6x is optically inexpensive for an engineering services company
key_risks: Operating margins of 9.04% — thin for a people-intensive business — are already compressing (operating income fell from INR 1,303 Cr in FY24 to INR 1,138 Cr in FY25, a 13% decline)
ROE of 12.8% is below my minimum threshold and has not improved meaningfully despite a decade of operations
Promoter holding of only 23.28% is uncomfortably low — limited insider alignment with long-term shareholders
red_flags: Net profit declined year-over-year in FY25 (INR 703 Cr to INR 648 Cr) — earnings are moving in the wrong direction
Other income declined from INR 140+ Cr historically to negative INR 2 Cr in FY24 — the earnings stream was partially propped up by non-operating items that have now normalised
Finance costs grew at 21.6% CAGR over 9 years, far outpacing the 10% revenue CAGR
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Cyient serves technically demanding clients in aerospace, defense, rail, and utilities — sectors where switching vendors is costly and relationships are sticky. Revenue has grown at 10.1% CAGR over nine years and the balance sheet is essentially debt-free. On the surface, this looks like a steady compounder. The problem is that engineering services without proprietary products are fundamentally people businesses where the main competitive tool is price.

The numbers confirm the structural limitation: 9% operating margins, 12.8% ROE, and now declining profits in FY25. The promoter's 23% stake means management does not suffer proportionally when returns are mediocre. At 19x current PE, I am not getting compensated for these shortcomings. A fair business at a fair price is not what I am looking for — I want a wonderful business at a fair price.
